Source: research/claim-ledger.yaml · no claim or evidence list is visually truncated
KNUDGE evaluates branching NPC dialogue against quest and entity
LLM proposals can be incrementally grounded by symbolic
validation for playable IF world generation.
The benefit of symbolic dialogue scaffolding can depend on NPC
role and does not universally improve player experience.
A recent 2026 preprint reports a perception-understanding gap
for engagement inference in the games it evaluates.
In the authored Stage 4 fixtures, the loader-enforced set
covered all 12 implemented error codes and observed outcomes
matched 13/13 authored expectations; this is authored-oracle
conformance, not an independent success rate.
Across the 12 authored initially-invalid repair cases at matched
budget K=1, rejection-only committed 0/12 and unchanged retry
5/12 and the state-reading policy-restore oracle committed 6/12;
every non-committing arm left the prior state hash unchanged.
Per frozen repairability class, guided repair committed 5/5
the oracle arm additionally committed the single oracle_only
case; guided commits used a mean changed-field edit distance of
1.0. This separates model-free counterexample repair from
state-reading repair on authored fixtures and is not a
All 10 faults prespecified as detectable were rejected by their

TRACE-RPG treats encoded hard predicates as a pre-commit gate
while narrative, affect, retrieval, and memory signals remain
Executed live screening pilot (gpt-5.6-sol via the Codex CLI, 5
seeds per cell, matched budget K=1, one proposal shared by both
arms). The guided-vs-blind separation is regime-dependent. On
the frozen offline base state the proposer returned 5/5
first-shot valid candidates with and without the constraint
table, because that state admits a zero-effect valid action, so
no repair was exercised; forbidding a zero-effect action there
produced 5/5 invalid candidates whose errors were all
QUEST_STAGE_REGRESSION, a guided-irreparable class, and both
arms committed 0/5. On the corrected signal-repair-v2 state with
the table withheld, live errors were POLICY_EFFECT_OMISSION,
guided repair cleared every error to commit 5/5 while blind
retry committed 0/5. Every fallback in every cell preserved the
In the live pilot, proposer errors co-occurred rather than
appearing singly, and a single guided-irreparable code blocked
commit even when the repairable codes were cleared. On the
superseded signal-repair v1 state the operator reduced the error
set from three codes to one (removing POLICY_EFFECT_OMISSION and
POLICY_EFFECT_VIOLATION) but could not commit because
NPC_KNOWLEDGE_VIOLATION remained, which the operator declines to
repair by contract. Per-error repair therefore does not compose
into a commit unless every co-occurring error is repairable at
